[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-018-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Deploy and Monitor Pages Internal Architecture | Studio: PlatformCore | Category: Architecture | Section: 1. Executive Summary | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: DeploymentManager, ModelMonitor, DriftDetector]

This document defines the AI-ConneX Deploy and Monitor Pages and the internal architecture that connects every approved artifact, model, recipe, manifest, agent, tool, telemetry stream and industrial endpoint into a deployable and observable runtime. The design supports edge, cloud and hybrid operation, with ONNX/ONNX Runtime for portable ML inference, MQTT for lightweight event/telemetry transport, REST APIs for synchronous application integration, and OPC UA where industrial equipment integration requires a standards-based industrial information model.

The central architectural principle is: BUILD ONCE → PACKAGE WITH IDENTITY → DEPLOY BY TARGET → VERIFY BEFORE SERVING → MONITOR CONTINUOUSLY → GOVERN CHANGES → ROLLBACK SAFELY.

ONNX Runtime is designed to run inference across cloud, edge and mobile environments and provides a common interface across multiple model frameworks and hardware accelerators. citeturn0search5turn0search9 MQTT 5.0 is a lightweight publish/subscribe protocol designed for constrained M2M/IoT environments. citeturn0search60 OPC UA provides industrial information models and communication mechanisms applicable to sensors, actuators, control systems, MES and ERP. citeturn0search6

Jane explains what is ready to deploy and why.

User selects an approved release, not an arbitrary artifact.

AI-ConneX resolves manifest, dataset contract, model, feature recipe, agent blueprint/runtime, tools and policy references.

Target planner determines edge/cloud/hybrid compatibility.

Pre-flight validation checks signatures, dependencies, resources, protocol configuration, health probes and policy.

Required human approval is requested.

Release is signed/registered and rollout begins.

Smoke tests and health checks run.

Telemetry must confirm readiness before the release is marked live.

[Governed Subsystems: DeploymentManager, ModelMonitor, DriftDetector]

Hybrid is the recommended default for industrial deployments where raw plant data should remain local while models, recipes, governance and aggregated telemetry may be managed centrally. The edge retains local operational capability; the cloud provides fleet governance, model lifecycle, cross-site analytics and centralized audit.

| Function | Edge | Cloud |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Raw sensor ingestion | Primary | Optional aggregate |
| Low-latency inference | Primary | Optional |
| Safety/plant-local policy | Primary | Central policy baseline |
| Model registry | Cached approved releases | Authoritative |
| Agent toolkit | Local subset | Fleet-wide |
| RAG | Local approved KB subset | Authoritative/global |
| Knowledge Graph | Local operational subgraph | Global graph |
| Telemetry | Buffer + forward | Central aggregation |
| Fleet monitoring | Local alarms | Central monitoring |

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-018-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Deploy and Monitor Pages Internal Architecture | Studio: PlatformCore | Category: Architecture | Section: 13. Protocol Architecture | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: DeploymentManager, ModelMonitor, DriftDetector]

MQTT 5.0 is appropriate for constrained and M2M/IoT scenarios because it uses publish/subscribe messaging and is designed for low-bandwidth environments. citeturn0search60 OPC UA is appropriate when semantic industrial information modeling and interaction with industrial systems are required. citeturn0search6

| Interface | Primary use | Pattern |
| --- | --- | --- |
| REST/HTTPS | Synchronous request/response, enterprise apps | API Gateway → Service |
| MQTT 5.0 | Telemetry, events, edge messaging | Publisher → Broker → Subscriber |
| OPC UA | Industrial data/model integration | Asset/PLC/SCADA/MES → Gateway |
| WebSocket/SSE | UI live status | Runtime → UI |
| Batch object storage | Large files/artifacts | Object store → worker |
| gRPC (optional) | Internal low-latency service calls | Service → Service |

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-018-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Deploy and Monitor Pages Internal Architecture | Studio: PlatformCore | Category: Architecture | Section: 14. MQTT Topic Architecture | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: DeploymentManager, ModelMonitor, DriftDetector]

ai-connex/{tenant}/{site}/{asset}/telemetry/{signal}ai-connex/{tenant}/{site}/{asset}/event/{event_type}ai-connex/{tenant}/{site}/model/{model_id}/predictionai-connex/{tenant}/{site}/agent/{agent_id}/statusai-connex/{tenant}/{site}/alert/{severity}ai-connex/{tenant}/{site}/deployment/{release_uid}/status

Use TLS and authenticated clients.

Use tenant/site authorization at the broker.

Use retained messages only where semantically appropriate.

Define QoS per message class.

Use message expiry for transient telemetry.

Do not put secrets or unnecessary PII into topic names.

Include event timestamp, sequence number, schema version and source identity in payloads.

For industrial ML, shadow and canary deployment are especially valuable because they allow the new model to be evaluated against live conditions before it becomes authoritative.

| Strategy | Use | Failure blast radius |

| Rolling | Routine stateless services | Medium |
| Canary | New model/agent version | Low |
| Blue-Green | High-confidence cutover | Low/medium |
| Shadow | Evaluate without affecting users | Very low |
| Edge Wave | Fleet deployment by site groups | Controlled |
| Offline Bundle | Disconnected plant | Local |

| Failure | Impact | AI-ConneX response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cloud dependency at plant | Operations stop during WAN outage | Local edge execution + buffering |
| Model/runtime mismatch | Inference failure | Compatibility manifest + pre-flight gate |
| Feature recipe mismatch | Silent prediction degradation | Feature contract versioning |
| Schema drift | Bad input | Schema monitor + gate |
| MQTT disconnect | Telemetry gap | Local buffer + reconnect + sequence numbers |
| Agent tool unavailable | Automation failure | Capability health + fallback/approval |
| Stale RAG/KG | Wrong recommendations | Knowledge freshness telemetry |
| Certificate expiry | Connectivity outage | Expiry monitoring + rotation |
| Bad release | Plant impact | Canary/shadow + automatic rollback gates |
| Resource exhaustion | Latency/crash | Resource quotas + admission checks |
| Tenant leakage | Severe security issue | Tenant-scoped identity, policy and storage |
| Observability failure | Blind operation | Local health + buffered telemetry |
| Clock drift | Incorrect event order | Time synchronization + source timestamps |
| Network partition | Partial system state | Explicit degraded mode |
| Agent loop runaway | Cost/latency/action risk | Budget, timeout, step limits |

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-018-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Deploy and Monitor Pages Internal Architecture | Studio: PlatformCore | Category: Architecture | Section: 24. How the Architecture Overcomes Them | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: DeploymentManager, ModelMonitor, DriftDetector]

The architecture separates control plane from data plane. The control plane manages desired state, releases, policies and fleet identity. The data plane executes inference, agents and industrial connectivity locally or in the selected runtime. This allows edge operation without requiring continuous cloud connectivity.

Security follows zero-trust principles: no implicit trust based on network location; identity and authorization are evaluated for users, devices and services. NIST SP 800-207 explicitly recommends protecting resources rather than trusting network location, while SP 800-207A describes application/service identity, API gateways and service-identity mechanisms for cloud-native multi-cloud systems. citeturn0search0turn0search1

Tenant-scoped authorization.

A tenant ID must never be accepted solely from a client-supplied body field. It should be derived from authenticated identity and server-side authorization context.

| Resource | Isolation rule |
| --- | --- |
| Artifact registry | Tenant namespace + authorization |
| Model registry | Tenant-scoped model IDs |
| Agent registry | Tenant/project scope |
| Telemetry | Tenant/site/resource labels + query enforcement |
| MQTT | Tenant/site ACLs |
| REST | Tenant claims enforced at gateway/service |
| Object storage | Tenant prefixes/buckets + encryption |
| Knowledge base | Tenant-scoped indexes |
| Knowledge graph | Tenant partition/subgraph |
| Edge node | Assigned tenant/site identity |
| Secrets | Tenant-scoped secret paths |

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-018-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Deploy and Monitor Pages Internal Architecture | Studio: PlatformCore | Category: Architecture | Section: 27. Edge Offline / Disconnected Mode | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: DeploymentManager, ModelMonitor, DriftDetector]

Pre-stage signed release bundles.

Cache model, feature recipe, agent package and required knowledge snapshot.

Continue local inference according to policy.

Buffer telemetry locally with bounded retention.

Queue non-critical cloud actions.

Block actions that explicitly require central approval.

On reconnection, reconcile telemetry and deployment state.

Detect conflicting desired state before applying updates.

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-018-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Deploy and Monitor Pages Internal Architecture | Studio: PlatformCore | Category: Architecture | Section: 35. POC — Industrial Compressor Health | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: DeploymentManager, ModelMonitor, DriftDetector]

A practical POC should deploy one vibration/temperature model to an edge node, publish sensor telemetry over MQTT, optionally ingest industrial context through OPC UA, expose predictions through REST, run an Agentic monitoring workflow, and show the complete lineage on Deploy and Monitor pages.

Compile/profiling stages create the manifest and feature contract.

ML Studio trains candidate models and exports the approved model to ONNX where supported.

Agentic Studio creates an approved monitoring agent SPEC and runtime package.

Deployment Control Plane creates a signed release.

Edge target passes pre-flight checks.

Model and agent are deployed in canary mode.

MQTT carries sensor events.

ONNX Runtime performs local inference.

REST exposes current prediction/status.

Monitor Page displays latency, model drift, asset health and agent status.

An induced MQTT interruption tests buffering/recovery.

An induced model degradation tests alerting/rollback logic.

Jane explains the incident using evidence from telemetry and lineage.

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-018-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Deploy and Monitor Pages Internal Architecture | Studio: PlatformCore | Category: Architecture | Section: 39. Closed-Loop Architecture | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: DeploymentManager, ModelMonitor, DriftDetector]

DEPLOY  ↓SERVE  ↓OBSERVE  ↓DETECT  ↓EXPLAIN  ↓USER / POLICY DECISION  ↓RETRAIN / RECONFIGURE / ROLLBACK  ↓VALIDATE  ↓REDEPLOY

The loop is deliberately governed. Monitoring may recommend a change; it should not automatically retrain and redeploy a critical industrial model unless an explicit policy permits that action.

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-018-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Deploy and Monitor Pages Internal Architecture | Studio: PlatformCore | Category: Architecture | Section: 43. Final Architecture Recommendation | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: DeploymentManager, ModelMonitor, DriftDetector]

AI-ConneX should implement Deploy and Monitor as two views over the same Release + Manifest + Telemetry graph rather than two independent applications.

This architecture joins the entire AI-ConneX pipeline: Jane → Brain → Data/ML/Agentic artifacts → Manifest → Release → Edge/Cloud runtime → industrial protocols → telemetry → monitoring → evidence → governed action. The industrialist sees a simple operational surface while the internal system retains deep technical control, lineage, observability and auditability.

| Deploy Page answers | Monitor Page answers |
| --- | --- |
| What am I deploying? | What is running? |
| Where will it run? | Where is it running? |
| Which model/agent/version? | Which version is actually serving? |
| What dependencies exist? | Which dependency is failing? |
| Is it safe/allowed to release? | Is it healthy/trustworthy now? |
| What is the rollout plan? | What happened during rollout? |
| How do I rollback? | Should I rollback? |
